transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I decided to come in because I just don’t feel any interest in the community projects and hobbies that used to mean everything to me. I used to be so active, but now I just feel completely blank when it comes to doing any of them.
Have you also been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, I have, but it's been going on for much longer than two weeks—ever since the accident over two years ago. It's like a heavy mix of guilt and dread sitting in my stomach like a dark cloud that just won't lift, even when I'm at church or with my grandchildren.
Have you had periods where your mood improved for more than a few weeks at a time since the accident, or has it been consistently low?
No, it has been consistently low without any real periods of improvement. That heavy cloud of guilt and dread has been with me constantly for over two years now, and it just hasn't let up at all.
Have you lost interest in almost all activities, including things you used to enjoy, nearly every day for most of the day?

Yes, absolutely. I used to live for my historic walking tours, the community garden, and even my weekly bowling night, but now I just stay home because I feel completely blank inside. It feels like there is no point in going anymore because I know I won't enjoy them like I used to.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F33", "F43"], but based on this conversation, F43 (reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders) seems less likely because the patient describes a persistently low mood lasting over two years without significant periods of improvement, which exceeds the typical duration and course of adjustment disorders. The chronic, unremitting nature of the depressive symptoms—such as profound loss of interest, persistent guilt, and anhedonia—starting after a stressful event but enduring far beyond it, aligns more closely with recurrent depressive disorder (F33) than with stress-related conditions. Therefore, the current candidate is F33.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent depressive episode lasting over two years following a traumatic event, without significant periods of mood improvement, meeting criteria for recurrent major depressive disorder, current episode moderate to severe. The absence of partial remission or symptom-free intervals supports the diagnosis of F33.1 rather than adjustment disorder.
